- KEM (RFC 9629 KEMRecipientInfo) recipients can now be used with CMS AuthEnvelopedData via the new org.bouncycastle.cms.jcajce.JceKEMAuthEnvelopedRecipient, the AuthEnveloped counterpart of JceKEMEnvelopedRecipient: it decapsulates the key-encryption key and verifies the AEAD authentication tag, so ML-KEM, FrodoKEM and Composite ML-KEM recipients work with AEAD content encryption (for example AES-256-GCM). Previously only EnvelopedData supported KEM recipients.

- The PQC private keys ML-DSA, ML-KEM, SLH-DSA, FrodoKEM and Classic McEliece (BCMLDSAPrivateKey, BCMLKEMPrivateKey, BCSLHDSAPrivateKey, BCFrodoKEMPrivateKey and BCCMCEPrivateKey in org.bouncycastle.jcajce.provider.asymmetric) now honour the JCA javax.security.auth.Destroyable contract. Previously destroy() fell through to the interface default, which throws DestroyFailedException, leaves isDestroyed() false and leaves the full secret recoverable via getEncoded() - so there was no way to erase these (comparatively large) private keys from the heap through the JCA API. destroy() now zeroizes the underlying key material (the corresponding org.bouncycastle.crypto.params.\*PrivateKeyParameters classes are themselves now Destroyable), isDestroyed() reflects the state, and getEncoded() and the other secret-bearing accessors throw IllegalStateException("key destroyed") afterwards. As the parameter arrays may be shared with keys derived from the original (for example via MLDSAPrivateKey.getPrivateKey(boolean)), destroying a key invalidates those references too (github #2366).
